Algebra I · Lesson 7.5

Intercepts and Standard Forms

Solve this lesson →All lessons

7.4 built a line from a point and a slope, and expanding the result left yy alone on one side, equal to a multiple of xx plus a constant. Only two numbers differ from one such equation to the next, the coefficient of xx and the constant term. The next two problems locate both of them on the graph.

Problem
The graph of y=4x−9y=4x−9 is a straight line, and this equation is already solved for yy. The line meets the yy-axis at exactly one point. Enter the yy-coordinate of that point.
Show a hint
  • From 7.2, every point of the yy-axis has x=0x=0. That point is on the line too, so its coordinates satisfy y=4x−9y=4x−9.
  • Replace xx with 00 in y=4x−9y=4x−9. The product 4(0)4(0) is 00, so the right side becomes a single subtraction from 00.
Show the full solution
Substituting x=0x=0 gives y=4(0)−9=0−9=−9y=4(0)−9=0−9=−9​. Reading the 99 without its minus sign gives 99 and puts the crossing above the origin instead of below it.
Problem
The line y=25x+6y=52​x+6 passes through the point with x=0x=0 and the point with x=10x=10. Work out the yy-coordinate of each, then use 7.3's definition to enter the slope of the line.
Show a hint
  • Substitute each xx into the equation to get the two points, then divide the change in yy by the change in xx.
  • At x=0x=0 the point is (0,6)(0,6), and at x=10x=10 the term 25(10)52​(10) is 44.
Show the full solution
At x=0x=0 the point is (0,6)(0,6) and at x=10x=10 it is (10,10)(10,10), so m=10−610−0=410=25m=10−010−6​=104​=52​​. The slope equals the coefficient of xx already written in the equation, and the constant term 66 is again the yy-coordinate at x=0x=0.
Key idea
Slope-intercept form. A line written y=mx+by=mx+b is in slope-intercept form. Substituting x=0x=0 gives y=by=b, so (0,b)(0,b) is a point of the line and bb is its yy-intercept. Substituting x=1x=1 gives a second point (1,m+b)(1,m+b), and by 7.3's definition the slope through those two points is (m+b)−b1−0=m1−0(m+b)−b​=m. Neither number has to be computed, which is why the slope worked out in the last problem was 2552​, the coefficient already written in the equation.
Problem
The equation y=−8x+13y=−8x+13 is already solved for yy, so the slope of its graph can be read straight off the equation without computing anything. Enter that slope.
Show a hint
  • The slope is the whole coefficient of xx, and the sign written in front of it is part of that coefficient.
  • Check with two points. Substituting x=0x=0 gives y=13y=13, and substituting x=1x=1 gives y=5y=5.
Show the full solution
The coefficient of xx is −8−8, so the slope is −8−8​. The points (0,13)(0,13) and (1,5)(1,5) give 5−131−0=−81−05−13​=−8 as well. A slope of 88 would mean yy rises as xx rises, and this line falls.
Problem
A line has slope −34−43​ and yy-intercept 1414, so its equation in slope-intercept form can be written down with no rearranging. Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is −12−12.
Show a hint
  • Putting m=−34m=−43​ and b=14b=14 into y=mx+by=mx+b gives the equation, and one substitution finishes it.
  • The equation is y=−34x+14y=−43​x+14, and at x=−12x=−12 the product −34(−12)−43​(−12) is positive.
Show the full solution
The line is y=−34x+14y=−43​x+14, and substituting x=−12x=−12 gives y=−34(−12)+14=9+14=23y=−43​(−12)+14=9+14=23​. Two negatives multiply to a positive, so the term −34x−43​x is 99 here and the result is larger than 1414, not smaller.
Key idea
Read mm and bb off the equation, signs included. In y=mx+by=mx+b the coefficient of xx is the slope and the constant term is the yy-intercept, and a minus sign in front of a number is part of that number, so y=−8x+13y=−8x+13 has slope −8−8 and y=6x−5y=6x−5 has yy-intercept −5−5. The two terms on the right may be written in either order, so y=11−2xy=11−2x and y=−2x+11y=−2x+11 are the same equation, with slope −2−2. The reading is valid only when yy is alone with coefficient 11, so 3y=6x−213y=6x−21 has to be divided through by 33 first, which gives y=2x−7y=2x−7.

Not every line is written with yy by itself. 7.2 wrote linear equations as ax+by=cax+by=c, both letters on the left, and that arrangement has its own name. Substituting 00 for either variable still leaves a one-letter equation, so the intercepts stay cheap, and one rearrangement is enough for the slope. The next two problems do one of each.

Problem
Exactly one point of the graph of 7x−4y=427x−4y=42 lies on the xx-axis. Enter the xx-coordinate of that point, not the point itself.
Show a hint
  • That point is the xx-intercept, so start by asking what the second coordinate equals at every point of the xx-axis.
  • Replace yy with 00 and simplify. The 4242 is divided by the coefficient of xx, not by −4−4.
Show the full solution
Substituting y=0y=0 gives 7x−4(0)=427x−4(0)=42, so 7x=427x=42 and x=6x=6​. Dividing 4242 by −4−4 instead gives −212−221​, which is where the line meets the yy-axis, not the xx-axis.
Problem
To find the slope of 4x+9y=634x+9y=63, solve the equation for yy and read the coefficient of xx. A student skips that and divides the coefficient of xx by the coefficient of yy as they stand, reporting 4994​. Enter the correct slope.
Show a hint
  • Reading the coefficients where they stand does not give the slope. Get yy by itself on one side first, and then the coefficient of xx is the slope.
  • Subtracting 4x4x from both sides gives 9y=−4x+639y=−4x+63. Now divide every term by 99.
Show the full solution
Subtracting 4x4x gives 9y=−4x+639y=−4x+63, and dividing every term by 99 gives y=−49x+7y=−94​x+7, so the slope is −49−94​​. The student's 4994​ is the negative of the correct slope, because subtracting 4x4x makes that term negative before the division by 99.
Key idea
Standard form. A line written Ax+By=CAx+By=C, with AA, BB and CC constants, is in standard form, which is 7.2's ax+by=cax+by=c in the usual capital letters. When B≠0B=0, subtracting AxAx from both sides gives By=−Ax+CBy=−Ax+C, and dividing every term by BB gives y=−ABx+CB,y=−BA​x+BC​, which is slope-intercept form. So the slope is −AB−BA​ and the yy-intercept is CBBC​. The minus sign is there because AxAx was subtracted first, not because of the division. Either constant may be negative, and 6x−2y=56x−2y=5 has B=−2B=−2 and slope 33.

Any line that has a slope can be written either way, and each direction is one short rearrangement. Standard form to slope-intercept form is solving for yy, which the last problem already did. The other direction means collecting both letters on one side and clearing any fraction, since AA, BB and CC are wanted as integers.

Problem
Write y=56x−4y=65​x−4 in the form Ax+By=CAx+By=C, where AA, BB and CC are integers with no common factor greater than 11 and A>0A>0. Those conditions fix the three values completely. Enter CC.
Show a hint
  • The three constants have to be integers, so clear the fraction first by multiplying every term by 66.
  • After multiplying, the equation is 6y=5x−246y=5x−24. Move the xx term to the left, then make the coefficient of xx positive.
Show the full solution
Multiplying every term by 66 gives 6y=5x−246y=5x−24, and subtracting 5x5x gives −5x+6y=−24−5x+6y=−24. Multiplying through by −1−1 makes A>0A>0, leaving 5x−6y=245x−6y=24, so C=24C=24​. The coefficients 55, −6−6 and 2424 have no common factor above 11, so with A>0A>0 this is the only such equation for the line.
Fun fact
Edmond Halley published a chart of the Atlantic in 1701, with a curve drawn through all the places where a compass needle pointed the same amount off true north. No printed map before it had shown lines of equal value.
Problem
Solve 14x+4y=914x+4y=9 for yy to put it in slope-intercept form. Enter the slope of the line, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Slope-intercept form needs yy alone with coefficient 11, so subtract the xx term first and then divide every term by the coefficient of yy.
  • The equation becomes 4y=−14x+94y=−14x+9. Dividing by 44 gives a coefficient of xx that is not yet in lowest terms.
Show the full solution
Subtracting 14x14x gives 4y=−14x+94y=−14x+9, and dividing every term by 44 gives y=−144x+94y=−414​x+49​, so in lowest terms the slope is −72−27​​. Reading −AB−BA​ straight off gives −144−414​, the same number, and it still has to be reduced.
Key idea
Solve for yy one way, clear the fractions the other. From Ax+By=CAx+By=C with B≠0B=0, subtract AxAx from both sides and divide every term by BB. From y=mx+by=mx+b, subtract mxmx to get −mx+y=b−mx+y=b, then multiply every term by a common denominator until no fraction is left. Multiplying both sides by the same nonzero number leaves the solution points unchanged, so 5x−6y=245x−6y=24 and 10x−12y=4810x−12y=48 are equations of one line. Requiring integers with no common factor above 11 and A>0A>0 leaves exactly one of them.

Substituting y=0y=0 in Ax+By=CAx+By=C leaves Ax=CAx=C, so the xx-intercept is CAAC​, and x=0x=0 leaves By=CBy=C, so the yy-intercept is CBBC​. That is 7.2's rule here, and each is one division. Exactly one line passes through two distinct points, so those two are the quickest pair to plot for a line in standard form.

Problem
The equation 6x=−156x=−15 is in standard form Ax+By=CAx+By=C with A=6A=6, B=0B=0 and C=−15C=−15. Enter the slope of its graph, or the word undefined if it has none.
Show a hint
  • The rule −AB−BA​ came from solving Ax+By=CAx+By=C for yy, and that step meant dividing by BB. Check whether that division can be done here.
  • There is no yy term, so the equation says x=−52x=−25​ and nothing about yy. Two points of the graph are (−52,1)(−25​,1) and (−52,4)(−25​,4), so work out the change in xx between them.
Show the full solution
With no yy term the equation is x=−52x=−25​, a vertical line, and every point of it has the same xx-coordinate, so the change in xx in the slope fraction is 00 and the slope is undefinedundefined​. The rule −AB−BA​ would give −60−06​, which is not a number, since that rule came from dividing by BB and is valid only when B≠0B=0.
Problem
The line 2x+9y=−362x+9y=−36 is in standard form, and it crosses the xx-axis at (p,0)(p,0) and the yy-axis at (0,q)(0,q). Enter the value of p+qp+q.
Show a hint
  • The two crossings come from two separate substitutions, y=0y=0 for the first and x=0x=0 for the second.
  • Setting y=0y=0 leaves 2x=−362x=−36, and setting x=0x=0 leaves 9y=−369y=−36.
Show the full solution
Setting y=0y=0 gives 2x=−362x=−36, so p=−18p=−18, and setting x=0x=0 gives 9y=−369y=−36, so q=−4q=−4, and their sum is −18+(−4)=−22−18+(−4)=−22​. Answering −18−18 reports only the xx-axis crossing, and dropping the minus on qq gives −14−14 instead.
Key idea
With B=0B=0 the line is vertical and the −AB−BA​ rule does not apply. Setting B=0B=0 in Ax+By=CAx+By=C leaves Ax=CAx=C, an equation with no yy in it, so from 7.2 the graph is the vertical line x=CAx=AC​. Every point of it has the same xx, so from 7.3 the slope is undefined. The step that produced −AB−BA​ was a division by BB, which is not allowed at B=0B=0. The line still has an xx-intercept at CAAC​, and it meets the yy-axis only when C=0C=0. With A=0A=0 instead the graph is horizontal, and there −AB=0−BA​=0 is correct.

Which form to use depends on the question. From standard form, each intercept is one division. From slope-intercept form, the slope and the value of yy at x=0x=0 are both readable with no work, and when yy is an amount changing at a constant rate as xx grows, from 7.3 those two numbers are the rate and the amount at the start.

Problem
Water runs into a tank at a steady rate. After xx minutes the tank holds y=112x+38y=211​x+38 liters. Enter how many liters the tank gains each minute.
Show a hint
  • The equation is already in the form y=mx+by=mx+b. The value of yy at x=0x=0 is the amount at the start, and the gain each minute is the change in yy when xx goes up by 11.
  • Work out what the tank holds at x=0x=0 and what it holds at x=1x=1. The difference between those two amounts is the gain in one minute.
Show the full solution
The equation is already in the form y=mx+by=mx+b, and the change in yy for each extra 11 of xx is mm, so the number of liters gained each minute is 112211​​. At x=0x=0 the tank holds 3838 liters and at x=1x=1 it holds 112+38211​+38, a difference of 112211​. The 3838 is the water in the tank before any ran in, so it is no part of the rate.
Problem
A line has slope −74−47​ and its xx-intercept is 1212. Written as Ax+By=CAx+By=C with AA, BB and CC integers having no common factor greater than 11 and A>0A>0, enter CC.
Show a hint
  • An xx-intercept of 1212 is the point (12,0)(12,0), so a point and a slope are both known and 7.4's point-slope form applies.
  • Point-slope gives y=−74(x−12)y=−47​(x−12). Multiply both sides by 44, expand the right side, then move the xx term across.
Show the full solution
From (12,0)(12,0) with slope −74−47​, point-slope gives y−0=−74(x−12)y−0=−47​(x−12), so 4y=−7x+844y=−7x+84 and 7x+4y=847x+4y=84, giving C=84C=84​. Here A=7A=7, B=4B=4 and C=84C=84 have no common factor greater than 11 and A>0A>0, so no rescaling is needed.

Each line here was taken on its own, and either form is enough to get its slope. With two lines at once there are further questions, whether they ever meet, whether they stay the same distance apart, and whether they cross at a right angle. Lesson 7.6, Parallel, Perpendicular, and Comparing Lines, answers all three by comparing the two slopes.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Enter the yy-intercept of the line y=3x+17y=3x+17, meaning the yy-coordinate of the point where the line crosses the yy-axis.
Show the solution
Substituting x=0x=0 gives y=3(0)+17=17y=3(0)+17=17​. In slope-intercept form y=mx+by=mx+b the constant term bb is the yy-intercept, so it can be read off without substituting.
Practice
Enter the slope of the line y=−58x+2y=−85​x+2.
Show the solution
The coefficient of xx is −58−85​, so the slope is −58−85​​. The 22 is the yy-intercept, not the slope.
Practice
Enter the slope of the line y=21−12xy=21−21​x.
Show the solution
Reordering gives y=−12x+21y=−21​x+21, so the slope is −12−21​​. The coefficient of xx is the slope whichever order the two terms are written in, and 2121 is the constant term, so it is the yy-intercept.
Practice
The line y=23x−5y=32​x−5 contains a point whose xx-coordinate is 1818. Enter that point's yy-coordinate.
Show the solution
Substituting x=18x=18 gives y=23(18)−5=12−5=7y=32​(18)−5=12−5=7​. The denominator 33 divides 1818 exactly, which is why an xx-value that is a multiple of the denominator keeps the arithmetic in whole numbers.
Practice
The equation 5y=35x−805y=35x−80 is not in slope-intercept form, since yy has a coefficient of 55. Rewrite it as y=mx+by=mx+b and enter the value of bb.
Show the solution
Dividing every term by 55 gives y=7x−16y=7x−16, so b=−16b=−16​. Reading −80−80 off the original equation is the common slip, since that constant still has to be divided by 55.
Practice
Enter the xx-coordinate of the point where the line 4x+9y=524x+9y=52 crosses the xx-axis.
Show the solution
Substituting y=0y=0 gives 4x=524x=52, so x=13x=13​. In standard form Ax+By=CAx+By=C that quotient is CAAC​, and the coefficient 99 of yy takes no part in it.
Practice
Enter the yy-coordinate of the point where the line 4x−7y=774x−7y=77 crosses the yy-axis.
Show the solution
Substituting x=0x=0 gives −7y=77−7y=77, so y=−11y=−11​. In Ax+By=CAx+By=C the yy-intercept is CBBC​. Here B=−7B=−7 and C=77C=77, so a positive CC still gives a negative intercept.
Practice
A student says the slope of 9x+8y=199x+8y=19 is 9889​, dividing the coefficient of xx by the coefficient of yy. Enter the correct slope.
Show the solution
Solving for yy gives 8y=−9x+198y=−9x+19, then y=−98x+198y=−89​x+819​, so the slope is −98−89​​. For Ax+By=CAx+By=C the slope is −AB−BA​ and not ABBA​, so the student's value has the wrong sign.
Practice
Enter the slope of the line 18x−4y=2518x−4y=25 as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Subtracting 18x18x leaves −4y=−18x+25−4y=−18x+25, and dividing every term by −4−4 gives y=92x−254y=29​x−425​, so the slope is 9229​​. The rule −AB−BA​ gives the same value, since A=18A=18 and B=−4B=−4 make −18−4=92−−418​=29​.
Practice
Write y=74x+12y=47​x+21​ in the form Ax+By=CAx+By=C, where AA, BB and CC are integers with no common factor greater than 11 and A>0A>0. Enter CC.
Show the solution
Multiplying every term by 44 gives 4y=7x+24y=7x+2, and subtracting 7x7x gives −7x+4y=2−7x+4y=2. Multiplying through by −1−1 makes A>0A>0, leaving 7x−4y=−27x−4y=−2, so C=−2C=−2​. Multiplying by 44 rather than by 88 keeps the coefficients free of a common factor.
Practice
The graph of 9x=−519x=−51 is a vertical line. Enter the xx-coordinate of the point where it crosses the xx-axis, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Dividing both sides by 99 gives x=−519x=−951​, and 5151 and 99 share the factor 33, so x=−173x=−317​​. Written as Ax+By=CAx+By=C this line has B=0B=0, so it has no slope and never meets the yy-axis.
Practice
The graph of 11y=−8811y=−88 is a horizontal line. Enter its slope, or the word undefined if it has none.
Show the solution
Dividing by 1111 gives y=−8y=−8, a horizontal line, and any two of its points have the same yy, so the change in yy is 00 and the slope is 00​. The rule agrees here, since −AB=−011=0−BA​=−110​=0, and it is allowed because B≠0B=0.
Practice
A cartridge holds VV milliliters of ink after printing pp pages, where 3p+2V=4803p+2V=480. Enter how many milliliters of ink each page uses.
Show the solution
Solving for VV gives V=−32p+240V=−23​p+240, and the size of the coefficient of pp is the milliliters lost per page, so each page uses 3223​​. The 240240 is the value of VV at p=0p=0, the ink in a full cartridge, and it is not the rate.
Practice
Enter the slope of the line 8y−3x=5y+248y−3x=5y+24.
Show the solution
Subtracting 5y5y gives 3y−3x=243y−3x=24, so 3y=3x+243y=3x+24 and y=x+8y=x+8, which has slope 11​. Reading −AB−BA​ off the original equation gives 3883​, which is wrong because the two yy terms had not been collected yet.
Practice
The line 7x+2y=427x+2y=42 crosses the two axes at two points. Those two points and the origin are the vertices of a right triangle. Enter its area.
Show the solution
Setting y=0y=0 gives x=6x=6 and setting x=0x=0 gives y=21y=21, so the legs have lengths 66 and 2121, and the area is 12(6)(21)=6321​(6)(21)=63​. The right angle sits at the origin, where the two axes meet and the two intercept distances are the legs.
Practice
The graph of kx+6y=23kx+6y=23 has slope 5335​, where kk is a constant. Enter kk.
Show the solution
The slope is −k6−6k​, so −k6=53−6k​=35​, and multiplying both sides by −6−6 gives k=−10k=−10​. Checking, −10x+6y=23−10x+6y=23 becomes y=53x+236y=35​x+623​, whose slope is 5335​.
Practice
A line passes through (−8,3)(−8,3) and (4,−6)(4,−6). Written as Ax+By=CAx+By=C with AA, BB and CC integers having no common factor greater than 11 and A>0A>0, enter CC.
Show the solution
The slope is −6−34−(−8)=−912=−344−(−8)−6−3​=12−9​=−43​, so from (4,−6)(4,−6), y+6=−34(x−4)y+6=−43​(x−4), and multiplying by 44 gives 4y+24=−3x+124y+24=−3x+12, so 3x+4y=−123x+4y=−12​. Moving the xx term the other way instead gives −3x−4y=12−3x−4y=12, where AA is negative, so 1212 is the wrong value to report.
